_about: Single source of a Wave model page's public facts. Build input only: not shipped. Pages render from it via {{card:<model>.<item>}} tokens (web/scripts/model-cards.mjs), so a number appears in exactly one place. Every measured item carries the R-number of the lab's results log and the date it was measured; ranges are published as ranges. Facts come only from the lab's UI handoff of 2026-10-20 and the release READMEs it names. To add a model page (Giga is next, when the lab supplies its facts): add an entry here with its page slug and status tier, build the page from the tokens, and add it to the Research menu, Models and status and the Wave family page; test/model-pages.test.mjs then holds it to the same rules. Status words (stage, band) are NOT here: they render from wave-status.json.

models.name: Wave Pico
models.author: RogerAI Labs
purpose: Reads one industrial telemetry channel at a time: Modbus registers, Sparkplug B, Prometheus, InfluxDB line protocol, Datadog series, syslog and feature summaries.
Names the instrument fault (stuck, dropout, noisy, drifting, railed, or none) or the process state the channel is in.
Answers only when its own confidence clears a measured gate. Below the gate it escalates, and an escalation is a record, not an answer.

limits.text: Root-cause chains read at chance. That is a larger tier's job.
Process state is its weakest family.
A healthy frame raises a false alarm on a small share of reads, independently from read to read. Integrate it with a three-read debounce.
The per-class calibration lifts tag truthfulness by recovering one class; the other class it covers stays at zero recall with or without it.
Fire numbers come from simulated fire scenarios with known answers. The fire adapter has not been read on real site data yet, and no site has recorded months of its own normal days.
The MLX build was checked on another backend. The run on a Mac with Metal is still owed.

models.name: Wave Nano
models.author: RogerAI Labs
purpose: Everything Wave Pico does: one telemetry channel in, the instrument fault or the process state out, behind the same kind of calibrated escalation gate.
Conversation, general questions, SQL and short technical writing, in a plain chat format.
Fleet reading as a parent node, the fire-site rollup, classifier reading of edge-AI payloads, and tolerance of damaged telemetry.

uses.title: A gateway reader.
uses.text: Rolls up many child nodes, resolves their conflicts and answers the mesh questions.

uses.title: A fire-site reader.
uses.text: The T17 rollup: site state, next action, which input decided, and what is inconsistent.

uses.title: A plant assistant.
uses.text: Explains a reading, writes a query, answers a question in plain words.

limits.text: General knowledge is weak at this size, 48.2 on our general macro. Do not use it as a reference.

On the public small-model suite (MMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag, IFEval and the rest) it is last in its size class on every task and at chance on MMLU and GSM8K. The industrial numbers above are where it leads; general knowledge, arithmetic and free-form instruction following are not.

A check on the training data found that about a third of the ARC prompts and a quarter of the IFEval prompts of the public suite had appeared, with answers, in the chat portion of the training data. On the prompts that had not appeared the readings sit within sampling error of the full-set numbers (IFEval 12.6 strict, ARC-Challenge 29.2), so the table keeps the full sets, which is what the other models were read on.
Sizing arithmetic without the calculator tool reads 17 to 20. The fire-decision adapter calls the calculator instead.
On real camera ticks, a camera margin that was over the line and fell below it over-alarms about 10% of the time, a tick shape the training set never held. A retrain that covers it is in training.
On real single camera ticks the misses are right decisions with an incomplete missing list, when the temperature feed is null.
The fire-decision adapter reads a tick by position. The caller writes every tick in one fixed key order before it asks.
The vision module reads single frames. The full watch design adds persistence and a per-camera baseline on top.
The vision numbers are on held-out frames from the camera networks it learned on, from one training seed.

Fire numbers come from simulated fire scenarios with known answers and from the served builds. The fire-decision adapter was also read on recorded camera readings from one installed site, with the other sensor feeds empty. No site has recorded months of its own normal days yet.
The MLX build for Apple Silicon is owed.

The vision module and the camera smoke detector it works with were trained in part on HPWREN archived data (CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial use under HPWREN’s no-fee Commercial Use Permission, registration filed by RogerAI). Data courtesy of HPWREN, University of California San Diego. FIgLib: Dewangan et al. (2022), Remote Sensing 14(4), 1007. HPWREN data are not intended for decision-making. The fire-decision adapter uses no HPWREN data.

parts.title: Chat.
parts.text: The base model on its own: telemetry, the fleet, the fire-site rollup, and conversation. On air as the free band wave-nano-chat.

parts.title: Fire sensor-reading adapter.
parts.text: Routed per request. Reads a fire site’s sensor frame: threat call, escalation, source, wind alignment and regime. Ships in the release; not on the band.

parts.title: Fire-decision controller adapter.
parts.text: Routed per request. Gives the site controller its decision from camera, chemistry and wind, plans its tool calls, names missing inputs, answers override requests, and steps back once a person acknowledges. On air as the free band wave-nano-fire-controller.

parts.title: Vision fire-confirm module.
parts.text: Nano-VL. After the camera detector alarms, it confirms smoke on the frame and describes it. On air as the free band wave-nano-fire-vision.
